newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - SBC has strong results, no surprises.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - SBC has strong results, no surprises.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) rounded out strong performances by Switzerland's biggest banks by announcing it had posted "excellent" first-quarter results that pushed its shares to a 1997 high.
Analysts said SBC was reaping the benefits of restructuring moves that all three big banks launched last year to deal with problem loans generated by the sluggish Swiss economy.
Banks also gained from extremely strong performances in securities markets, so the outlook for the rest of the year will depend partly on how markets fare, they said.

SBC registered shares touched a high of 341.00 Swiss francs, up 11, after reporting first quarter net after taxes and minorities was above expectations and results were strong. As usual, SBC provided no numbers with the report.
It also said it was confident that it would reach goals set for 1997, but was not more specific.

An SBC spokesman said it was referring to targets it set last September projecting 1.7 billion Swiss francs ($1.2 billion) in net profit for 1997 and a medium-term return on equity goal of 15 percent.
"We are basically still positive. We see further potential. There were no surprises," said Daniel Hauselmann, equities analyst at UBS.

"It (the good result) is based on extremely good financial markets, which created a lot of volume. The second part is that provisions were slightly lower this year, which is providing benefits," he said.
"What I also found very positive is that the costs were clearly lower. The cost/income ratio has clearly improved."
Claudia von Tuerk, equities analyst at Pictet & Cie, said it was unfortunate that the bank does not provide more detailed figures, but added: "The first quarter has been excellent."
She expected the banking group to continue to show a strong performance "even if the rest of the year is not too good".
"Revenues are up while costs are under control, which is the ideal constellation," she said.
Pictet is forecasting 1.68 billion Swiss francs in net profits for 1997, close to SBC's own target of 1.70 billion. Pictet is also forecasting 1998 net of 1.88 billion.
"It depends so much on what the markets are going to do. We are taking a relatively conservative stance," von Tuerk said.
Commissions were expected to be strong in 1997, even if markets do not boom, given a good increase in assets under management already seen in 1996, she said.

"The big question is trading income. There we are forecasting a decline versus 1996. The thing is, you never know what is going to happen. If the markets do not provide a (negative) surprise, we could be overly conservative," she said.
But if securities markets continue to boom, she said, this would not only increase trading returns but would increase staff costs tied to bonuses paid.

Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said last month it posted excellent operating results in the first quarter, with group profit and cash flow rising strongly from the year-earlier period. Ideal market conditions boosted earnings significantly.

Credit Suisse Group said this week it was confident of hitting mid-term financial goals after getting off to a very good start in the first quarter, when revenue from lending, commissions and trading rose significantly.
Expenses and provisions developed in line with management expectations, the group said.
-- Zurich newsroom +41 1 631 7340 ($ = 1.442 Swiss Francs)
